fields.sample_size: 84 municipalities of Hidalgo state, Mexico (3,083,841 inhabitants): municipal water tariffs (CAASIM and state official gazette 2022), INEGI household environment module (MOHOMA 2017: mean weekly bottled-water spending of 51.74 pesos, deflated), CONAGUA concession register (REPDA 2022) and the 2020 census; no household survey
fields.effect_measure: municipal affordability index: average household water spending (tariff plus bottled water) as a percentage of household income, taking one or two minimum salaries, against the 3% UNDP affordability threshold; water availability per inhabitant by municipality; descriptive maps and counts
fields.effect_estimate: In 2020, 96% of the population of Hidalgo had piped water (66.9% inside the dwelling, 29.1% within the plot; 80% from the public service and 15.7% from community wells) and 94% sewerage; coverage is lowest in Huautla (65.2%), La Misión (68.4%), Yahualica (72.8%) and Tepehuacán (75.3%); 50.8% of the population is poor and 11.8% indigenous; water pressure is medium-strong (32.3%). With one minimum salary of household income, average water spending exceeds the 3% threshold in the municipalities mapped (highest Tianguistengo 12.5%, Nicolás Flores 10.5% and Jacala de Ledezma 10%), so households are vulnerable under the human right to water mainly because of tariffs and bottled-water costs; the state has the most agricultural wastewater discharge points in Mexico and weak sectoral regulation. The author recommends local public-policy strategies to reduce the financial and health effects.
fields.section: Full text (Spanish, 21 pages, Agua y Territorio 24:169-189): Introduction; Method (affordability formulas, data sources); the water of Hidalgo (coverage, concessions); results on affordability (Map 4); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Method (formulas for average household water spending and the 3% criterion); section on water in Hidalgo (coverage by municipality); Map 4 and Conclusions; Agua y Territorio 24:169-189

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a documentary and secondary-data analysis of water sufficiency and affordability in the 84 municipalities of Hidalgo under the human-right-to-water framework (tariff plus bottled-water spending against a 3% income threshold); read in full text 2026-10-04. Descriptive; spending figures depend on assumed incomes of one or two minimum salaries.
